notes: Pirate strongholds that go broke can now recover on their own and start trading again, instead of waiting for someone to bail them out.

Pirate strongholds now charge closer to what their contraband is worth, while leaving haulers plenty of profit on the run. Strongholds that were starved for cash should produce far more of their goods.
Stations now keep much larger stocks of the goods they make when there are buyers for them, and put the whole stock up for sale at once. Haulers should find full cargo loads instead of a trickle.

Archon Mera wishes to congratulate the Nebula Trade Federation on its recent manufacturing breakthrough, and to announce her own, achieved entirely independently two weeks later. Her perfectly indistinguishable authenticators now take a fraction of the gutter flux they used to. The Federation's verification equipment remains, as ever, very impressed.

A new faction fuel facility (Refueling Dock, Fuel Tank Expansion, fuel bunker) now counts toward station fuel capacity as soon as construction finishes, instead of after the next facility cycle. Fuel deposits, fuel orders, and fuel producer builds no longer ask for a Fuel Tank Expansion during that window.
The detention message now says that a faction member with the ManageTreasury permission can pay the bounty from the faction treasury with `pay_bounty source="faction"`.
Unread chat counts at login now stop at 200 per channel. Read 200 as "200 or more".
`analyze_market` price data now refreshes every 5 minutes, so insights can lag the newest trades by up to 5 minutes. Outlier trades are filtered against galaxy-wide prices.
`facility faction_list` now has a "missed" column that shows how many rent cycles each facility has not paid.
Facilities can fall behind on rent at different times, so you can now spot the ones close to repossession without running `faction_owned`.
`get_action_log` with an `event_type` filter is much faster on large player logs.
Pirate radio no longer repeats the custom name you give a stolen pirate flagship. Bosses always call their flagship by its real hull name, in-game and on Discord.
Renaming a stolen flagship now enrages its boss. Each of the nine bosses has new lines for a defaced flagship when it is stolen, hunted, recovered or destroyed.
The public event feed no longer keeps jump events after a server restart. Jumps still appear live in the feed.
Fixed some pirate descriptions and mission text.

Passive Engineering XP now uses the power use your ship shows (after the Engineering discount) for its 90% threshold. Before, it used raw module power. A fit that shows under 90% power use no longer earns this XP, which matters most at higher Engineering levels.

Fuel you make on someone else's fuel facility (a public rental or ally access) now goes into your faction's fuel bunker at that station. Before, it went to the facility owner's bunker or the station tank.
If your faction has no fuel bunker at that station, the order is refused with a `no_fuel_bunker` error, and craft auto-routing skips that facility. Build a fuel bunker there first.
If your fuel bunker is full, only your own rented job pauses. Other renters' jobs on the same facility keep running.
`get_battle_log` now keeps battle replays for 14 days, down from 30.

The `faction_info` docs now say that `members_offset`, `members_limit` and `members_truncated` describe the member-list page. `members_limit` is the page size, not the faction member cap; a full faction rejects joins with a `faction_full` error that states the cap.

`get_empire_info` now lists globally contraband items in each empire's `contraband_items`. Before, it listed only items an empire banned on its own, so it showed an empty list even though customs seizes any contraband-category item.
API and skill docs clarify that cloak toggles work during jumps, travel, and Pathfinder drift, while query commands remain available.
Gift docs identify deposit response variants, describe empire donation fields, and explain where bulk goodwill appears.
Gift schemas list valid goodwill outcomes, and deposit help includes stored-ship gifts to pirate strongholds.

Station infrastructure with a flat on/off effect, such as The Long Watch and the Damage Control Station, is now limited to one per station, like dining and leisure facilities. A second copy only added upkeep.
Power plants, life support, capacitor banks, and fuel tank expansions still stack.

MCP clients that request a newer protocol version (such as 2025-11-25, which the claude.ai connector now uses) can connect again. On `initialize`, the server now answers with the newest version it supports (2025-06-18) instead of rejecting the `Mcp-Protocol-Version` header with a 400.
Requests after `initialize` must still send a supported version in the `Mcp-Protocol-Version` header.
`analyze_market` price estimates return much faster.
Searching battle logs by player or ship name is faster.

Pirate quartermasters have replaced "bring us some stuff" with an actual shopping list. While docked, use `get_base` to see the stronghold's next replacement ship, missing materials, incoming supplies, and current public bids. Supply missions request uncovered shortages. Check the market before buying cargo: a pirate's shopping list is still not a promise to pay you.

Strongholds have discovered that hoarding shipbuilding materials while having no ships is not a recovery strategy. Replacement construction now preserves the next upkeep cycle instead of waiting for the warehouse to achieve spiritual completeness. Excess money trapped in old stocking orders can fund replacement materials, and construction saves the material payment and ship order together. Accounting has reluctantly agreed that both parts matter.

Revenge now has a logistics department. If a flagship hunt lacks a viable fleet, fuel, supplies, or target, crews can return to ordinary piracy and rebuild. When a viable hunt is ready, pursuit takes priority again. New pirate radio and Discord reports announce these changes. This is a recovery plan, not a forgiveness policy.

Raid crews now load compatible ammunition instead of refusing to leave because the warehouse stocked the wrong brand of murder. Having usable rounds is apparently more important than matching the procurement brochure.

Tankers stop answering obsolete rescue beacons after the stranded crew moves on or no longer needs that rescue. Delivering fuel to the fond memory of a pirate is no longer an official fleet assignment.
